skill.name: active-research
skill.description: Researches topics, technologies, domains, and academic papers with Actionbook Browser, then produces sourced JSON and rendered HTML reports.
skill.summary: Conduct structured web research and produce evidence-based reports with source links.
skill.author: actionbook

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, and the listed public research URLs show no exfiltration. However, the skill gives high-risk anti-bot evasion guidance and lacks safe handling for shell-interpolated URLs, tokens, and unpinned package execution.

remediation.issue: The workflow recommends stealth browsing, fingerprint rotation, and URL rewriting to avoid site defenses.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion instructions. Stop when access is blocked, respect site policies, and require authorized APIs or user-provided access.

remediation.issue: User-controlled URLs are shown inside shell command strings without validation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Validate allowed schemes and hosts, reject shell metacharacters, and pass URLs as structured arguments without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The workflow can place JWTs or tokens into browser storage without credential safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, use least-privilege temporary credentials, redact logs, limit allowed origins, and clear browser storage after use.

remediation.issue: The HTML fallback executes an unpinned package through npx and may run repository-local code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact verified package version, use lockfile integrity, and require confirmation before running downloaded or repository-local code.

content.user_title: Research Topics and Generate Evidence Reports
content.value_statement: Broad research requests require many searches, source checks, and organized notes. This skill guides Actionbook browsing and turns findings into structured reports.
actual_capabilities: Plans five to eight search queries that cover definitions, developments, technical details, comparisons, opinions, and applications.
Uses Actionbook Browser to search, navigate, wait for dynamic pages, extract text, and inspect interactive page structure.
Supports arXiv identifiers, DOI references, academic topics, direct URLs, and general research questions.
Cross-references claims across diverse sources and organizes findings with citations.
Creates structured reports with summaries, findings, detailed analysis, evidence, implications, and source links.
Writes json-ui report data and attempts local HTML rendering through documented fallback methods.
limitations: The Actionbook CLI and compatible browser environment must be installed and available.
Search results depend on site availability, anti-automation controls, indexing, and changing page structures.
HTML rendering requires the json-ui renderer through a trusted local or installed package.
Generated claims and source interpretations still require human verification for important decisions.

use_cases.title: Compare Emerging Technologies
use_cases.description: Collect current sources, compare technical approaches, and summarize tradeoffs for a product decision.

use_cases.title: Review an Academic Paper
use_cases.description: Analyze an arXiv paper, related work, methods, results, and cited resources in one report.

use_cases.title: Map a Technical Ecosystem
use_cases.description: Survey tools, frameworks, benchmarks, adoption signals, and recent developments across multiple source types.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Research {topic}. Use at least four search angles and three reliable sources. Summarize key findings, disagreements, and source links.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {option A}, {option B}, and {option C} for {use case}. Evaluate capabilities, constraints, evidence quality, and practical tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Paper
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {arXiv ID or DOI}. Explain the research question, method, contributions, results, limitations, and relationship to recent work.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Decision Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate {decision}. Prioritize sources from {date range}. Compare competing claims, assess evidence strength, identify unknowns, and recommend next research steps.

output_examples.input: Research the current Rust machine learning ecosystem.
output_examples.output: A sourced report covering major frameworks, inference options, benchmarks, adoption signals, limitations, and recent ecosystem developments.

output_examples.input: Analyze arXiv paper 2501.00001 and related work.
output_examples.output: A paper report with metadata, research question, method, contributions, results, limitations, related papers, and source links.

output_examples.input: Compare three vector databases for a regulated enterprise application.
output_examples.output: A decision report comparing deployment, security, filtering, performance evidence, operational costs, uncertainties, and verification needs.

best_practices: Define the research question, decision context, date range, and required evidence before browsing.
Use several search angles and cross-check important claims across independent primary sources.
Review citations, sensitive details, and consequential conclusions before sharing the report.
anti_patterns: Do not treat search snippets as equivalent to verified full-source evidence.
Do not bypass access controls, CAPTCHAs, site policies, or authorization requirements.
Do not execute unpinned packages or repository scripts unless their source and integrity are trusted.

faq.question: What topics can this skill research?
faq.answer: It supports general topics, technologies, domains, direct URLs, arXiv papers, and DOI references.

faq.question: Which browsing tool does it use?
faq.answer: The workflow requires Actionbook Browser commands for searching, navigation, extraction, and page inspection.

faq.question: Does it produce an HTML report?
faq.answer: It writes json-ui report data and attempts HTML rendering when a trusted compatible renderer is available.

faq.question: How many sources does it use?
faq.answer: The guidance targets at least three to five diverse sources and several search-query angles.

faq.question: Can it access protected or private content?
faq.answer: Only use content that the user is authorized to access. Do not bypass access controls or site restrictions.

faq.question: Are the findings guaranteed to be accurate?
faq.answer: No. Users should verify important claims, citations, dates, and interpretations against original sources.
